'''Irina Mitrea''' is a Romanian-American mathematician who works as professor and department chair at the Department of Mathematics of [[Temple University]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=People - Department of Mathematics at Temple University|url=https://math.temple.edu/people/|access-date=31 March 2021|website=[[Temple Mathematics]]}}</ref> She is known for her contributions to [[harmonic analysis]], particularly on the interface of this field with [[partial differential equation]]s, [[geometric measure theory]], [[scattering theory]], [[complex analysis]] and [[validated numerics]]. She is also known for her efforts to promote mathematics among young women.<ref name="girls">{{citation|url=https://temple-news.com/lifestyle/summer-math-camp-boys-allowed/|title=For summer math camp, no boys allowed: Mathematics professor Irina Mitrea runs a summer-camp for girls only|newspaper=[[The Temple News]]|first=Claire|last=Sasko|date=August 26, 2014}}.</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=WPI to Host Mathematics Day for Middle and High School Girls|url=https://www.wpi.edu/news/math|access-date=2021-03-31|website=WPI|date=20 November 2009 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Girls and Mathematics Summer Day Program {{!}} Institute for Mathematics and its Applications|url=https://www.ima.umn.edu/2010-2011/SP6.20-24.11/|access-date=31 March 2021}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=AWM Service Award 2015|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-service-award/awm-service-award-2015/|access-date=31 March 2021|website=[[AWM Service Awards 2015 - Association for Women in Mathematics]]}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Mitrea earned a master's degree from the [[University of Bucharest]] in 1993,<ref name="michler"/> and completed her doctorate in 2000 at the [[University of Minnesota]] under the supervision of [[Carlos Kenig]] and Mikhail Safonov. Her dissertation was ''Spectral Properties of Elliptic Layer Potentials on Non-Smooth Domains''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=60676}}</ref>  Her publications include over fifty research articles and three books published by [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer‐Verlag]], [[Birkhäuser]], and [[De Gruyter]].<ref name=":1" />  After temporary positions at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and [[Cornell University]], she joined the faculty of the [[University of Virginia]] in 2004, and earned tenure there in 2007.<ref name="michler"/> She also taught at the [[Worcester Polytechnic Institute]] before moving to Temple.<ref>{{citation|title=Math Quiz: Why Do Men Predominate? It's culture, not biology|journal=[[IEEE Spectrum]]|first=Prachi|last=Patel|date=November 30, 2009|volume=46 |issue=12 |page=22 |doi=10.1109/MSPEC.2009.5340245|bibcode=2009IEEES..46l..22P |s2cid=27126159|url=https://spectrum.ieee.org/math-quiz-why-do-men-predominate|quote=Irina Mitrea, a math professor at Worcester Polytechnic Institute, in Massachusetts, who finished high school in Romania, says she never felt discouraged there: 'In fact, being good at math made you popular.'}}</ref> She is the founder of the Girls and Mathematics Program at Temple University, a week-long summer camp in mathematics for middle-school girls.<ref name="girls"/> She is a member of the National Alliance for Doctoral Studies in the Mathematical Sciences, an organization providing mentorship to "build a national community of students, faculty, and staff who will work together to transform our departments, colleges, and universities into institutions where all students are welcome."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Irina Mitrea {{!}} Math Alliance: The National Alliance for Doctoral Studies in the Mathematical Sciences|url=https://mathalliance.org/mentor/irina-mitrea/|access-date=2021-09-28|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-09-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928222035/https://mathalliance.org/mentor/irina-mitrea/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2008, Mitrea won the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]] of the [https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/ Association for Women in Mathematics].<ref name="michler">{{cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/ruth-i-michler-prize/michler-prize-2008-2009/|title=Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize 2008–2009|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|access-date=31 January 2021}} Also printed in [http://www.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/pubs/may08web.pdf ''MAA Focus'' 28(5), May/June 2008], [[Mathematical Association of America]], p.&nbsp;5.</ref> In 2014, she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to partial differential equations and related fields as well as outreach to women and under-represented minorities at all educational levels."<ref name="ams">[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, retrieved 2015-01-18.</ref> Also in 2014, Mitrea was awarded a [[Von Neumann Fellowship]] at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]].<ref name=temple>{{cite web|title=Temple Mathematics News 2014|url=https://math.temple.edu/news/2014/|access-date=31 January 2021}}</ref> In 2015 she received the AWM Service Award from the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref name=":0" /> She is part of the 2019 class of fellows of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2019-awm-fellows/|title=2019 Class of AWM Fellows|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|access-date=2019-01-26}}</ref>
